newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude firm in active speculative trading.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude firm in active speculative trading.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures shook off a weak opening and were firmer across the board, with products also unexpectedly firmer after an attmept to push the complex through support levels failed, traders said.
At 1134 EDT, July WTI was up 13 cents at $22.03 a barrel. Spot June, which expires today and was seeing steady liquidation volume, was up 13 cents at $21.72.
Heating oil prices were also higher. June heat had reversed early losses and was up 0.38 cent to 58.30 cents a gallon, erasing most of Monday's profit-taking losses.

Unleaded gas was higher in the front months, weaker in the back months with good industry demand seen supporting values as the sector began to separate slightly from the complex, according to trader said.
"Gas held up well after the inventory numbers last week and the demand seems to be there," he said.
This week's American Petroleum Institute status report - with stocks, output, imports, capacity utilization etc - is due out Tuesday after market's close.
A Kurdish rebel group attacked an oil installation in southeast Turkey as conflict there continued to rumble along, but NYMEX traders said the marekt was focusing mainly on technical trading Tuesday.

Selling pressure at the opening bell from speculators to force a move below support levels failed almost immediately, dealers said. They said trade and refiners were buying July and vying for lots needed by locals and speculators to turn over June positions, as well as spreads.
The June/July spread had narrowed to 39 points from Monday's close at 49 points.
"Just like yesterday, when we blew out a lot of the longs, today we're taking out a lot of shorts, once we held the early dip," one floor broker said.
July crude resistance was put at $22.40/50.
